data.title: The disruptive applications of AI: still hidden in the corners
data.description:
Recently, at the APEC summit, Lei Jun, when discussing the current development of AI, mentioned (paraphrased):

The development of large-scale AI models has been rapid over the past four years, but industry investment is large, application scenarios are limited, and few companies have achieved profitability. He pointed out the harsh challenges that current AI development brings to enterprises.

In the various AI fields I understand, currently, apart from a very few application areas (such as ByteDance's Red Fruit short dramas) and hardware and contract manufacturing companies (such as Nvidia, TSMC, and some component companies), many companies are forced into an arms race that they have no choice but to participate in, investing heavily but seeing no returns in the short term.

Even top large-scale model companies (such as Anthropic) have achieved amazing revenue growth in their enterprise-facing businesses, but this is still a drop in the ocean compared to the computing power expenditures they will have to invest in the future. It will take some time for revenue to fully cover expenses and achieve a completely positive cash flow.

The substantial profits of already profitable hardware and contract manufacturing companies are also driven by the expected expenditures of large-scale model companies.

Large-scale model companies dare to invest heavily because they have seen the potential of superintelligence, especially in mathematics, physics, and biology. Under such extremely attractive expectations, the entire industry, especially the capital market, is willing to pay for such extravagant spending. In some areas that have generated positive cash flow, although individual applications (such as Red Fruit Short Drama) appear to have generated cash flow, the vast majority of short video creators in the entire field are still losing money. Therefore, this profit model may not be easily replicated or imitated by other companies. Furthermore, I believe that for AI, a disruptive technology, short videos are certainly not disruptive applications. Essentially, they only upgrade and improve the efficiency of the existing (video) industry, without changing the industry's production relations and profit distribution relationships. Therefore, this application is likely only temporary and may be replaced and disrupted by new AI video applications in the future. Overall, in the current AI ecosystem, what people are most confident in and certain of is the foundation of the entire ecosystem—large-scale models and related hardware supply chains. It not only determines the foundation for the future growth of a country/ecosystem, but also its very lifeline. Therefore, capital from all sectors is pouring into this field, whether actively or passively. This reminds me of the early development of the crypto ecosystem: After Ethereum launched in 2015, the following two years saw the value and potential of smart contract public chains. Thus, in the ICO boom of 2017, the vast majority of projects, especially those with astonishing funding, were smart contract public chains. These projects aimed to create Ethereum killers, aiming to monopolize the foundation of the entire ecosystem. At that time, ecosystem participants paid little attention to application areas, nor were they able to. This was not only because people couldn't see any specific application areas that could generate real-world applications and revenue; it was also because people were convinced that once they secured dominance in the smart contract public chain foundation, they could share in the monopolistic profits regardless of any future applications. However, that fierce competition for funding ultimately ended in disaster, with 99.99% of ICO public chains failing. Conversely, peripheral applications, which had been relatively inconspicuous during the subsequent bear market, became the leaders of the DeFi boom and the infrastructure for applications across the entire crypto ecosystem today. This round of AI competition may follow a similar path, with most competitors focusing on large-scale models failing, leaving only a very few. Meanwhile, the currently inconspicuous peripheral applications may become giants and infrastructure in new application areas in the future.

data.title: Will Bitcoin hit a new high next year? Top 10 trends in the crypto market in 2027.
data.description:
Source: 21shares

Compiled by: Kaozai

As we approach the end of 2026, the AI ​​investment boom is in full swing, the Middle East conflict remains unresolved, and signs of a potential debt crisis in the Eurozone are emerging. US economic growth is led by technology, but inflation is above target, and interest rates continue to rise. In other economies, energy supply shocks have driven up inflation without generating corresponding growth; credit spreads are widening as financing costs rise.

Digital assets have withstood the test in this environment.

Bitcoin has fallen more than 50% from its October 2025 high, and the Clarity Act has failed to reach a consensus. However, this asset class has begun a K-shaped recovery, with several sub-sectors experiencing a new round of price discovery thanks to stronger fundamentals. Four main drivers are at play: Demand for value storage: Rising debt, high inflation, and persistently high interest rates are prompting investors to reassess Bitcoin's status as a native internet store of value, with more and more people allocating it alongside gold. A convergence in tokenization: Even though the Clarity Act has not yet been passed, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) have issued relevant frameworks and definitions, laying the foundation for the settlement of real-world assets on the blockchain.

Shifting to 24/7 Trading: Sudden market shocks and demand for pre-IPO asset exposure highlight the value of 24/7 trading venues; traditional exchanges like the CME Group are also moving towards 24/7 trading.

Privacy Protection and Quantum Defense: Concerns about AI-driven surveillance make privacy technologies more necessary; quantum resistance is now on the agenda for digital assets and critical national infrastructure.

21shares believes that 2027 will be the year the market prices "resilience." The following ten predictions outline the next phase: 21shares' expectations, the data supporting those expectations, and the conditions needed for those expectations to come true. ...>

Each prediction is an opinion formed by 21shares based on data up to October 2026 and is not a prediction of investment returns. For any asset allocator, the biggest question is: will central banks continue to tighten policy or shift to easing as growth weakens? Prediction 1: Bitcoin will reach a new all-time high, but the cycle peak has not yet been reached. Bitcoin fell from a high of approximately $126,000 in October 2025 to a low of $59,000 in June 2026, but buying did not stop. Since 2024, ETFs, corporations, and sovereign institutions have absorbed a total of 1.75 million Bitcoins, worth approximately $145 billion at current prices. During the bear market alone, they added 180,000 coins, while 122,000 coins were mined during the same period (Source: 21shares, Glassnode, Farside, BitcoinTreasuries.net, as of October 6, 2026). Large brokerages and 401(k) retirement plans are also continuously expanding their investor base. Historical cycles provide a reference. The increase from cycle lows to highs has narrowed from 114 times to 21 times, and then to 8 times; while in previous cycles, after each bottoming out 12 months ago, the price of Bitcoin reached at least 2.2 times the low. If this pattern is applied to the low point in June of this year, Bitcoin is expected to return to its previous high by mid-2027. The next halving will occur in 2028, and the past three cycles all peaked approximately 18 months after the halving. Therefore, 21shares believes that 2027 will not be the peak of this cycle. This judgment also has limitations. The sample size of the three cycles is very small, and past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results. Bitcoin has already fallen by more than 50% in this cycle, and it may repeat itself in the future. Some investors hold Bitcoin to hedge against currency devaluation, viewing it as a scarce asset not controlled by any government, but this argument remains controversial. Prediction 2: Digital Asset Regulatory Rules Go Global For most of the development of the crypto industry, US policy has been primarily manifested through litigation and enforcement actions. Since 2024, regulators have approved spot ETFs, dropped cases against several large blockchain companies, abolished regulations that excluded banks from custody services, and the federal stablecoin law, the GENIUS Act, has been signed into law. Regulatory systems in the EU (MiCA, Crypto Asset Market Regulation Act), Japan, Canada, Brazil, Turkey, and other regions have already been implemented, while systems in the UK and Australia are expected to be implemented in 2027. 21shares predicts that, including the US and South Korea, 15 of the 21 G20 members will have established relevant systems. The US regulatory framework is taking shape step by step. Although the CLARITY Act failed to reach a consensus in September, many of its agendas do not rely on the act: The GENIUS Act will officially take effect next January. The SEC has opened a five-year window for tokenized stocks and is expected to finalize safe harbor rules for tokens in 2027. The CFTC is developing rules for perpetual contracts and prediction markets. A federal digital asset tax framework has been passed by the committee by a vote of 38 to 5. The Federal Reserve, the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC), and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (FDIC) have confirmed that eligible tokenized securities are subject to the same bank capital treatment as traditional forms of securities. This provides the long-awaited legal basis for custodians, exchanges, and stablecoin issuers, as well as banks, investment advisors, and pension funds. It should be noted that the above statistics are 21shares' judgment and do not represent that all relevant legislation has been passed. The situation in South Korea shows that a single controversy—whether banks or technology companies should issue stablecoins in the Korean won—is enough to bring the entire market to a standstill. Prediction 3: Stablecoin Monthly Active Addresses Exceed 100 Million Stablecoins are digital assets designed to be pegged to the value of currencies such as the US dollar. In September 2026, the number of monthly active stablecoin addresses reached 76.4 million, and monthly bank card spending by the Neobank digital asset project reached $1.22 billion (data source: 21shares, Paymentscan, Visa Onchain Analytics, Allium). 21shares predicts that the number of active addresses will exceed 100 million in 2027, and annual bank card spending will reach $25 billion. It's important to note that the number of addresses is not the same as the number of users; this figure should be considered a metric for activity. Distribution channels are playing a crucial role: PayPal's Hyperwallet supports payments in PYUSD, Western Union has launched a Visa card backed by a stablecoin, and Stripe's Bridge supports USDC payroll payments for World App. Recipients can receive digital dollars without changing their existing banking habits. Whether this prediction will materialize depends on user retention beyond early incentives like cashback; furthermore, RedotPay's data is self-disclosed and cannot be verified on-chain. Prediction 4: Real-world assets and fintech will account for 15% of total DeFi revenue. Decentralized finance (DeFi) has long suffered from two major shortcomings: limited product offerings and a focus on trading, coupled with a lack of customer support when problems arise. Fintech applications are addressing the first shortcoming: Robinhood Earn offers yield products from Morpho, while Phantom and MetaMask provide leveraged equity exposure powered by Hyperliquid. Currently, real-world assets and fintech distribution channels account for approximately 8% of total DeFi revenue, and 21shares projects this figure will reach 15% by the end of 2027. Regulatory support is also in place: the SEC's five-year conditional exemption allows eligible tokenized US stocks to trade on permissioned platforms, and banking regulators have clarified their capital treatment methods. Some of Coinbase's tokenized assets are already available as collateral on Aave. Thus, traditional assets can support lending and liquidity on blockchain infrastructure, while the user experience is handled by fintech applications. Prediction 5: Tokenized Asset Trading Volume to $15 Trillion 21shares predicts that the trading volume of tokenized real-world assets in the spot and perpetual contract markets will increase from $6.3 trillion in 2026 to $15 trillion in 2027. Its quarterly trading volume has already increased from $0.12 trillion in the first quarter to $2.6 trillion in the third quarter. Three landmark moments in 2026 highlight demands that traditional trading venues cannot meet: Precious Metals (January): During traditional market closures, the daily trading volume of silver perpetual contracts exceeded $1 billion. Crude Oil (February): Following the US-Iran military strikes, Hyperliquid reflected approximately 80% of oil price fluctuations before traditional exchanges even opened. Pre-IPO Equity (May-June): SpaceX's perpetual contracts were launched weeks before the company's IPO; upon listing, its stock opened at a price closer to the contract's implied value, rather than the $135 offering price set by the underwriters. To reach $15 trillion, a compound annual growth rate of approximately 21% per quarter is needed starting from the third quarter, while this growth rate is expected to reach approximately 357% by 2026. The CME Group's push for 24/7 trading in digital assets and gold indicates that traditional institutions are also responding to the same demand. Prediction Six: On-chain Options Trading Volume Exceeds $100 Billion. Options are one of the largest markets in traditional finance, with an average daily notional trading volume of approximately $4 trillion. In contrast, the on-chain options market remains small: 21shares estimates it at around $30 billion in 2026, with quarterly trading volume increasing from $2.1 billion in Q4 2025 to $8.8 billion in Q3 2026. As the development path of perpetual contracts repeats itself in the options space, 21shares expects on-chain options trading volume to exceed $100 billion in 2027. The founder of Hyperliquid stated that options are the platform's next frontier; Lighter has also launched binary options. The maximum loss for an options buyer is limited to the premium paid, so drastic price fluctuations will not lead to forced liquidation—unlike the deleveraging in October 2025, where forced liquidations exceeded $19 billion within 24 hours. Options can also be used for risk hedging and building structured yield products; traditional users need these tools to move large positions on-chain. Prediction 7: The prediction market is poised to reach $1 trillion, but new strategies are needed. Driven by sporting events, the prediction market is projected to surpass $500 billion in trading volume by 2026. With the World Cup attracting a large number of traders, Kalshi and Polymarket's monthly trading volume roughly doubled between May and July, increasing from $26 billion to $53 billion. Without events of similar scale, 21shares expects its growth rate to slow to below 150%, but its annual trading volume is still expected to exceed $1 trillion. This requires a monthly average trading volume of $83 billion, meaning a higher, more consistent trading base is needed, rather than relying on occasional spikes in volume. The risks are also concentrated. Sports-related transactions accounted for a staggering 79% of July's trading volume; the CFTC is defending its federal regulatory authority, while some states are challenging sports contracts based on gambling laws, and several countries have already begun banning such platforms. Short-term contracts and financial contracts are the main pathways for predicting market breakthroughs in the sports sector. Prediction 8: The market capitalization of privacy-related assets has tripled from $4 billion at the end of 2024 to approximately $31 billion, accounting for about 1% of the $2.6 trillion digital asset market excluding stablecoins. 21shares predicts that its market capitalization will exceed $100 billion in 2027. If it can capture 5% of the market share, its market capitalization will reach approximately $130 billion. Three forces support this judgment: Investor security: According to CertiK statistics, there were 72 violent attacks against digital asset investors in 2025 and 52 in the first half of 2026. AI surveillance: AI models are absorbing more and more personal and financial data, and privacy tokens can keep on-chain balances and payment information encrypted. Institutional demand: If they cannot obtain the same level of privacy as traditional markets, institutions will not move large positions on-chain. Backed by over 30 institutions, Canton processes over $8 trillion in tokenized assets monthly. Since the market peaked in October 2025, ZEC and XMR have risen by 467% and 52% respectively, while BTC and ETH have fallen by 32% and 43% respectively. The privacy sector is the only digital asset sector to surpass its previous high, indicating that market expectations are already high. Prediction Nine: Privacy AI and Blockchain-Powered AI Take Center Stage. 21shares predicts that smart agent finance (i.e., transactions, lending, and payments conducted on-chain by AI agents) will break through the crypto-native user base in 2027. AI agents cannot open bank accounts without human approval, but they can hold digital assets 24/7. Robinhood's Agentic Accounts and Coinbase's Agentic Wallets already support AI models for transactions, and the x402 payment protocol has processed over 234 million transactions. However, activity levels fluctuate significantly. x402's monthly transaction volume peaked at 69 million in November 2025, fell below 4 million in early 2026, and has since recovered to approximately 13 million. Privacy-preserving inference is equally important in this area: the intelligent agents acting on your behalf require precisely the information you least want to reveal. Venice AI, a privacy-focused product that can replace mainstream models and does not store any user data, has seen its user base grow from approximately 450,000 in January 2025 to over 5 million. Prediction 10: Exchanges will transfer 50,000 Bitcoins to addresses hiding public keys. The US requires critical infrastructure in sectors such as defense, banking, and healthcare to achieve quantum security by 2030. Bitcoin exposes its public key when spent, and a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could potentially deduce the private key from the exposed public key. Approximately half of the Bitcoin held by exchanges faces this threat. 21shares predicts that by the end of 2027, the total amount of Bitcoin exposed will reach 7.5 million, and service providers will transfer at least 50,000 Bitcoins to addresses hiding public keys. This figure represents approximately 5% of their risk exposure, but would mark the first shift in custody practices. Currently, such a quantum computer does not exist. IonQ estimates that a hypothetical 2028-level device could crack a Bitcoin private key in 26 days; similarly, custodians need time to test new wallets and securely transfer assets. The ten largest Bitcoin ETF issuers in the US have all disclosed quantum risks in their filings with the SEC. Coinbase plans to upgrade its signature system in mid-2027, a noteworthy milestone, but no custodian can make Bitcoin quantum-safe on its own. A more fundamental solution lies at the Bitcoin protocol level, with proposals such as BIP-360 under discussion. Conclusion: Digital Assets Are Integrating into the Financial System Familiar to Investors

Looking beyond individual predictions, the top ten predictions share a common theme. Bitcoin's market capitalization has shrunk by more than half, yet the amount absorbed by buyers still exceeds three times the new supply. Regulators in major global economies are shifting from enforcement-based regulation to rule-based regulation. Stablecoins, tokenized assets, and 24/7 trading venues are being embedded in everyday payment applications, brokerages, and banks. Even emerging fields like on-chain options and AI agents have quantifiable usage data to support their growth; and custodian institutions have begun to address quantum risks before the threat looms large.

Conclusion: Digital Assets Are Integrating into the Financial System Familiar to Investors

Looking beyond individual predictions, the top ten predictions share a common theme. Bitcoin's market capitalization has shrunk by more than half, yet the amount absorbed by buyers still exceeds three times the new supply. Regulators in major global economies are shifting from enforcement-based regulation to rule-based regulation. Stablecoins, tokenized assets, and 24/7 trading venues are being embedded in everyday payment applications, brokerages, and banks. Even emerging fields like on-chain options and AI agents have quantifiable usage data to support their growth; and custodian institutions have begun to address quantum risks before the threat looms This is precisely what 21shares refers to as "resilience." Digital assets are no longer starting from scratch and building a parallel system, but are integrating into the existing system that investors already rely on—21shares predicts that the market will price this shift in 2027. However, this does not mean the risks have disappeared. Prices remain highly volatile, regulatory implementation paces vary, and some predictions depend on user retention after incentive reductions. Please treat each prediction as a viewpoint to be tested, not a conclusion to be copied and pasted. The full report details the data, sources, and conditions required for each of the ten predictions.

data.title: Binance founder CZ talks about prediction markets: The future potential is huge.
data.description: On November 27th, at the BNB Hackathon, an audience member asked Binance founder CZ: "Have you been following prediction markets? Could you tell me how big you think the future ceiling for prediction markets is?" CZ shared his assessment of this sector. CZ: Prediction Markets Have Huge Future Potential The following is a transcript of the Q&A: Audience Question: Have you been following prediction markets? Could you tell me how big you think the future ceiling for prediction markets is? CZ: I think it has a lot of potential, but I don't know how quickly it will reach that point. Prediction markets have historically been suppressed because people viewed them as gambling. In many countries, people confuse prediction markets with gambling. But things are different now. The US is legalizing some prediction markets and issuing licenses, and many projects are migrating to blockchain. Therefore, I believe this sector will experience significant growth. Compared to its future potential, the current prediction market is still quite small. Prediction markets are strongly event-driven, making them ideal for promotion, such as elections and the World Cup—events that attract widespread public attention. Compared to trading, it leans more towards the attention economy. Therefore, I think the prospects are very good.

data.title: The Bitcoin mining survival battle: Some shut down mining farms, while others turn to AI.
data.description:
Tao Zhu, Jinse Finance

Summary: In 2026, the cryptocurrency market continued its downturn, with Bitcoin prices falling from their highs, resulting in reduced mining profits for miners. Affected by multiple factors such as the sluggish market, electricity costs, and equipment depreciation, some mining farms shut down, while some mining companies turned their attention to AI… The cryptocurrency mining industry is undergoing a major reshuffle.

I. The Downturn in Cryptocurrency Markets Impacts Miners

In 2026, the overall performance of the cryptocurrency market was poor, with Bitcoin prices continuing to be under pressure, significantly impacting miners.

According to CoinGecko data, the price of BTC was at a high of $97,000 in January of this year, but fell to a recent low of $58,800 on November 21, a drop of 39.38%.

Bitcoin miners' income mainly comes from block rewards and transaction fees, while operating costs include electricity, mining machine purchase and maintenance, site rental, labor, and financing costs. When the price of Bitcoin rises, miners can earn income by selling the mined BTC; however, when the price of Bitcoin continues to fall, mining income will shrink, but costs will not decrease in tandem, and continuous losses will lead to a wave of miner shutdowns.

On November 23, according to F2Pool's mining machine revenue data, based on a BTC price of approximately $60,590 and an electricity price of $0.06 per kilowatt-hour, all Antminer S19 series mining machines were operating at a loss.

On November 23, according to F2Pool's mining machine revenue data, based on a BTC price of approximately $60,590 and an electricity price of $0.06 per kilowatt-hour, all Antminer S19 series mining machines were operating at a loss.

The Antminer S19 XP had a shutdown price of $66,089 and a daily net profit of -$0.36. The Antminer S19 Pro and S19 had daily net profits of -$1.56 and -$1.98 respectively, with shutdown prices of $90,824 and $105,154 respectively. The Whatsminer M60 and M66 had a shutdown price of approximately $61,170, with electricity costs accounting for 101% of their total cost, placing them below the break-even point.

II. Decreasing Hashrate and Lower Mining Difficulty

The Bitcoin network determines who gets the right to record new blocks through hashrate competition. The more hashrate miners contribute, the higher the network hashrate, and the more intense the competition for mining blocks.

On September 15th, Coinshares released the "Bitcoin Mining Report | Q2 2026": In Q2 2026, the overall cash flow of the publicly traded mining industry fell below the break-even point. Bitcoin closed the quarter at $58,400, less than half of its all-time high in October 2025; in June, the average monthly hashrate price fell to a record low of $27.7/PH/s/day. In Q2 2026, the weighted average pre-tax cash cost for publicly traded miners to produce one Bitcoin was approximately $75,500.

Due to the continued sluggishness of the cryptocurrency market, mining machines have shut down, the network's hashrate has decreased, and the block generation speed has slowed down. As a result, the network has lowered its mining difficulty: On November 15, according to The Defiant, Bitcoin completed a difficulty adjustment at block 975,744, decreasing from 148.36T to 134.82T by 9.13%, which is the largest drop since June and the third largest drop this year.

Due to the continued slump in the cryptocurrency market, mining machines have shut down, the network's hashrate has decreased, and the block generation speed has slowed down. As a result, the network has lowered its mining difficulty: On November 15, according to The Defiant, Bitcoin completed a difficulty adjustment at block 975,744, decreasing from 148.36T to 134.82T by 9.13%, which is the largest drop since June and the third largest drop this year.

... The average block time for the first 2,016 blocks was 11 minutes, with a cycle time of approximately 15.4 days. The estimated hashrate dropped to approximately 965 EH/s, a deeper decline than the predicted 6.8% to 7.5%. Bitcoin fell to $67,652 during the same period, putting pressure on miners: daily production on November 8th and 9th was only 346,875 coins (normally 450), the 7-day average Puell multiple was 0.82, and the daily value of 0.71 was the lowest since August 11th; transaction fees showed no improvement. The expected revenue per unit of hashrate increased mechanically by about 10% after the difficulty reduction, but the difficulty is still about 8% higher than the June low. Whether this can alleviate the situation depends on the return of hashrate. The decrease in mining difficulty means that miners do not need to invest as much computational work as before to have the opportunity to obtain the same block rewards. With Bitcoin price, transaction fees, and total network hashrate remaining unchanged, a 9.13% decrease in difficulty means that the expected block reward per unit of hashrate increases by about 10%. This provides a certain profit margin for mining machines that are still running, and also allows some previously shut-down mining machines to be restarted. The recent hashrate price is also worth noting. Hashprice, or "hash rate," is an important indicator of a Bitcoin miner's profitability. It represents how many US dollars a miner can theoretically earn per day for every 1 PH/s (quadrillion hashes per second) of hashrate invested. Hashrate price is mainly affected by three factors: Bitcoin price: The higher the BTC price, the higher the US dollar income for mining the same amount of Bitcoin. Mining difficulty and network hashrate: The higher the difficulty and the larger the network hashrate, the less block reward a single miner typically receives. Transaction fees: In addition to block subsidies, miners also receive transaction fees generated within blocks. Therefore, a decrease in the price of computing power means a reduction in miners' revenue per unit of computing power, squeezing their profit margins. According to Hashrate Index data (https://hashrateindex.com/blog/hashrate-index-roundup-november-23-2026/), on November 23, the price of computing power in USD changed by -3.0%, from $30.27/PH/s/day to the current $29.36/PH/s/day.

Bitcoin Hashrate Price Index (USD) | Weekly View (November 16, 2026 - November 23, 2026)

Besides the price of Bitcoin and the total network hashrate, transaction fee revenue is also an important factor affecting the profitability of miners. Bitcoin miners' income mainly consists of block rewards and transaction fees. Block rewards are a fixed BTC reward that miners receive after successfully mining a new block, while transaction fees depend on users' demand for block space.

From November 16th to 22nd, miners received approximately 3434 BTC in block rewards, worth about $214 million. However, transaction fee revenue during the same period was only about 22 BTC, accounting for approximately 0.64% of the block rewards. This means that miners' income is still highly dependent on block rewards, and transaction fees have not yet become an effective supplement to their revenue. Furthermore, industry insiders have predicted that the next Bitcoin mining difficulty adjustment may increase by about 9%, from 134.82T to approximately 147T. This means that the breathing space provided by the difficulty reduction in mid-November may be significantly compressed. For Bitcoin miners, the reduction in mining difficulty is only a temporary buffer. What truly affects their revenue is the price of Bitcoin and various costs. Miners with high electricity costs, low mining machine efficiency, and insufficient capital reserves will be essentially incurring continuous losses if they continue mining under the current circumstances.

III. Bitcoin Miners: Shutting Down or Transforming

Amidst the decline in Bitcoin prices and shrinking mining profits, miners are adopting different strategies. Some companies are choosing to completely exit the Bitcoin mining field and reinvest their funds in their original core businesses; others are beginning to transform towards AI.

1. KULR Technology Group: Refocusing on the Battery Sector>

KULR Technology Group (NYSE: KULR) is a US-based thermal management and battery safety technology company listed on the NYSE, serving the aerospace, electronics, and electric vehicle industries. Since 2024, the company has adopted a BTC reserve strategy and has been involved in Bitcoin mining.

In July 2026, KULR decided to exit the Bitcoin mining business and cease all mining activities by July 31st.

According to the company's 2026 Q3 10-Q filing with the SEC, KULR's mining rig leasing agreement with Pow.re expired on July 30 and was not renewed. On August 4, KULR reached an agreement with Soluna to terminate the remaining mining rig leasing contract early, paying a $150,000 early termination fee. KULR stated that exiting the mining business is an important part of the company's strategic adjustment. Previously, Bitcoin mining accounted for approximately 43% of its total revenue in 2025, but the company has now decided to refocus its operations on its core battery technology business, developing energy management services through the KULR ONE battery infrastructure platform. 2. Keel Infrastructure: Shifting Towards High-Performance Computing and AI Infrastructure On November 5th, according to Keel Infrastructure's quarterly earnings report, the company sold 2,520 bitcoins in the third quarter, raising $192 million, including all 2,261 bitcoins in reserves and 259 bitcoins mined during the quarter. Its Moses Lake facility ceased mining in April, while its Panther Creek, Scrubgrass, and Sharon facilities ceased operations on June 29th. As of September 30th, the company's bitcoin holdings were negligible. Keel stated that it will sell bitcoins mined daily from its Quebec operations; the company, formerly Bitfarms, is shifting its focus to high-performance computing and AI infrastructure. 3. Core Scientific: Shifting Towards High-Performance Computing and AI Infrastructure Core Scientific, one of the world's leading Bitcoin mining companies, is gradually transforming its traditional mining facilities into AI and high-performance computing data centers. On November 5th, Core Scientific released its third-quarter financial report. The company's third-quarter revenue reached $233 million, of which data center hosting revenue was approximately $215 million and Bitcoin mining revenue was approximately $17.5 million. The company previously signed a long-term cooperation agreement with AI cloud computing company CoreWeave and further established business partnerships with AMD and related Neocloud companies, involving approximately 530 megawatts of data center capacity. According to Core Scientific's Q3 2026 10-Q filing with the SEC, as of September 30, the company was still operating proprietary mining rigs at two facilities and providing hosted mining services to one customer. Management stated that the Bitcoin mining business will cease operations on December 31, 2026. During the earnings call on November 5, management stated that they expect to complete the exit from the Bitcoin mining business by the end of 2026 and will primarily operate as a high-density data center hosting service provider in 2027. 4. IREN: Shift to AI IREN stated in its 10-K annual report that its transformation from mining to artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to be largely completed by December 31, 2026. In the latest quarter, the company recorded a $450.4 million impairment charge for obsolete mining hardware and a $102.1 million write-down of mining rigs to be sold. Additionally, IREN listed a $25.1 million loss on disposal of assets. Notably, its AI cloud revenue ($70.5 million) surpassed mining revenue ($66.7 million) for the first time. Currently, IREN does not hold any Bitcoin (almost all of its daily Bitcoin production is sold). 5. TeraWulf: Shift to AI TeraWulf is further accelerating its transformation to AI. In the first half of 2026, the company's two mining facilities in Lake Mariner were shut down, resulting in a $25.7 million impairment charge on mining assets, and the remaining assets had their useful lives shortened accordingly. Currently, high-performance computing (HPC) leasing revenue accounts for 71% of TeraWulf's total revenue; correspondingly, disclosures about its mining operations have decreased—the 179 bitcoins mined in the second quarter were neither mentioned in its press releases nor on conference calls, but were only disclosed in its 10-Q quarterly report. 6. HIVE: Shift to GPU Cloud Services In October of this year, Bitcoin mining company HIVE Digital Technologies, through its subsidiary BUZZ HPC, transformed its mining infrastructure into GPU cloud services. In June, the company signed a three-year, approximately $220 million agreement with Bell AI Fabric to deploy 2,304 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs for Cohere; in August, it signed a five-year, approximately $350 million agreement with an unnamed company for 2,016 GB300 GPUs, totaling approximately $570 million. HIVE plans to build a 320-megawatt AI Gigafactory in the Toronto area, scheduled to begin operations in the second half of 2027, with an investment of approximately C$3.5 billion.

data.title: Standard Chartered-Owned Zodia Custody Suffers Data Breach Exposing Client And Employee Names And Emails
data.description:
Zodia Custody, the cryptocurrency custody business owned by Standard Chartered, has disclosed a security breach that exposed limited client and employee information, raising fresh concerns about cybersecurity as the bank expands its digital asset operations.

The London-based firm confirmed that an unauthorised party accessed some business information after suspicious activity was detected on its platform.

However, the company said its investigation had found no unauthorised transactions or evidence that the exposed information had been used for phishing or impersonation.

Reuters: Standard Chartered’s Crypto Custody Unit Zodia Suffers Security Breach

According to Reuters, Standard Chartered’s crypto custody unit Zodia Custody suffered a security breach this week, exposing client and employee data, including names and email addresses. Zodia… pic.twitter.com/QjlgLHAAQz

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 26, 2026

How Did Hackers Gain Access To Zodia Custody's Systems?

Zodia detected attempts to probe its platform on 23 November 2026 and temporarily shut down its business-to-business (B2B) application programming interface (API) as a precaution.

The API allows institutional partners to connect their systems directly to Zodia's custody platform.

The company introduced additional security measures before restoring the service.

By 24 November, its investigation had confirmed that an unauthorised party had accessed limited client and employee information.

Zodia subsequently contacted affected clients and notified the relevant regulators.

Chief Executive Richard Clark explained the response in a statement on 26 November 2026.

"On November 23, we detected attempts to probe our platform. As a precaution, we temporarily took our business-to-business (B2B) API offline and implemented additional security measures before restoring the service."

We are aware of media reports regarding a recent security incident. Richard Clark, CEO of Zodia Custody:

"On 23 November, we detected attempts to probe our platform. As a precaution, we temporarily took our B2B API offline and implemented additional security measures before…

— Zodia (@ZodiaCustody) November 26, 2026

What Client And Employee Information Was Exposed?

The exposed information included publicly available organisation details.

For a small number of clients and employees, it also contained business contact names and email addresses.

Zodia reported no evidence that the information had been used for phishing or impersonation attempts.

It also found no unauthorised movement of client assets.

Clark said,

"Based on our investigation to date, there have been no unauthorised transactions."

The company said its investigation was continuing.

Standard Chartered's Full Takeover Of Zodia Comes Amid Security Breach

The incident comes weeks after Standard Chartered signed definitive agreements on 21 October 2026 to acquire 100% of Zodia Custody, expanding the bank's involvement in the digital asset sector.

The acquisition remains subject to regulatory approvals.

Launched in 2020 as a joint venture between Standard Chartered's SC Ventures and Northern Trust, Zodia also counts SBI Holdings, National Australia Bank and Emirates NBD among its backers.

The firm supports more than 70 digital assets and operates in regulated markets including Singapore, Hong Kong, Australia, the United Arab Emirates and Luxembourg.

Under the restructuring plan, Zodia's regulated custody operations will be integrated into Standard Chartered's Securities Services business, while its technology infrastructure and professional services operations will be separated into an independent company called Zodia Solutions under SC Ventures.

The breach adds to the cybersecurity challenges facing financial institutions as they expand their digital asset services.

It remains unclear whether artificial intelligence or other advanced tools played any role in the incident.

data.title: Taiwan's Stablecoin Rules: Bank-led, Full Reserves, and Dual Approval
data.description: Mobile Payment Network News: Recently, Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) officially published a draft of the "Regulations Governing the Issuance and Management of Stablecoins" in the Executive Yuan Gazette. Along with eight supporting subsidiary laws for virtual asset service providers disclosed simultaneously, this marks the transition of Taiwan's stablecoin regulation from a general legal framework to the stage of implementing detailed rules. The draft will be open for public comment until December 16th, allowing for a 40-day consultation period. The FSC has clearly stated that all nine supporting subsidiary laws are planned to be finalized by the end of the first quarter of 2027 and implemented simultaneously with the "Virtual Asset Service Act." This is the most substantial institutional implementation in the stablecoin field since the Virtual Asset Service Act was passed in June of this year, directly establishing the entry threshold, issuance rules, and industry structure for the local stablecoin market in the coming years. From Fundamental Law Principles to 36 Implementable Rules The draft "Measures for the Licensing and Management of Stablecoin Issuance" disclosed this time contains 36 articles. It transforms the fundamental requirements of the parent law regarding stablecoin issuance licensing, asset preparation, redemption mechanisms, and information disclosure into a set of regulatory rules covering the entire process from issuer qualifications and application approval to reserve custody and internal control audits. Contrary to previous market expectations, this draft does not adopt a generalized approach to financial technology openness. Instead, it firmly anchors issuance rights within the traditional financial system from the outset, forming an access structure of "banks as the main body, non-banks as the supplement, and strict binding." The eight supporting sub-laws for virtual asset service providers disclosed simultaneously also set differentiated entry thresholds for crypto asset businesses with different risk levels: the minimum paid-in capital for virtual asset exchange, transfer, and underwriting businesses is NT$50 million; for trading platforms and custody businesses, it is NT$100 million; and for lending businesses, it is NT$200 million. An additional operating margin mechanism is also established, requiring custodians to set aside 2.5% of the balance of customer virtual assets held by their clients as operating margin. Financial institutions engaging in virtual asset business adopt a gradual opening strategy, initially only allowing banks with actual experience in virtual asset custody to undertake related businesses. Exchange and transfer services are initially limited to corporate clients. This arrangement clearly shows the regulatory authorities' logic: first, complete the licensing of existing crypto platforms, and then gradually open up permissions to the high-risk stablecoin issuance stage. The most significant innovation in this draft is that, through a three-tiered structural arrangement, stablecoins are redefined from "quasi-crypto assets" to "quasi-payment financial instruments," fully integrating them into the existing financial regulatory and monetary control system. The first innovation is the bank-led issuance threshold design. The draft clarifies three types of institutions eligible to apply for stablecoin issuance: local banks, financial holding companies, or joint-stock companies invested in by banks that meet capital adequacy requirements and have not had any major regulatory deficiencies in the past year, as well as other institutions to be separately announced by the Financial Supervisory Commission in the future. The draft law imposes dual shareholding constraints on non-bank issuers: the combined shareholding of a financial holding company and a bank must exceed 50%, and at least one financial holding company or bank must hold more than 25% of the shares individually. It also requires non-bank issuers to meet a minimum paid-in capital of NT$300 million, a public offering obligation, and a monopoly requirement. This arrangement means that non-financial technology companies and crypto institutions cannot independently apply for issuance licenses and must enter the market through a bank-controlled route, fundamentally preventing institutions lacking financial compliance experience from directly controlling stablecoin issuance rights. Secondly, it mandates 100% full reserves and a domestic trust custody mechanism. The draft requires issuers to maintain sufficient reserve assets, ensuring that the total value of reserves measured at fair value is never less than the total outstanding stablecoin balance. Furthermore, reserve assets must be completely segregated from the issuer's own assets, entrusted to a domestic financial institution to establish a dedicated trust account for independent custody, and establishing a regular accounting reconciliation mechanism between the issuer and the trustee bank. Combined with the bankruptcy remoteness clauses explicitly stated in the parent law—namely, "holders have priority in receiving payment from the reserve assets, and the reserve assets are not included in the issuer's bankruptcy estate"—this design fully aligns with the current reserve regulatory standards of mainstream markets such as Hong Kong, the United States, and Singapore. Furthermore, its additional emphasis on the requirement that "all reserve assets are held in financial institutions within Taiwan" further strengthens the controllability of monetary sovereignty and capital flows. Thirdly, there is a dual approval mechanism involving the central bank's consent and the Financial Supervisory Commission's permission. This is the most distinctive arrangement in the global stablecoin regulatory framework, and even in other East Asian economies such as Japan and South Korea, a similar design has not yet appeared. This setting directly elevates the regulatory focus of stablecoins from the regulation of ordinary financial products to the level of monetary and payment system security. It means that any stablecoin issuance must simultaneously meet the dual requirements of financial prudential supervision and monetary liquidity management, eliminating the risk of potentially disrupting the local monetary order from the source of approval. In addition, the draft also clarifies several bottom-line rules: stablecoins are only allowed to be pegged 1:1 to the New Taiwan Dollar or a single foreign currency, and a basket of currencies is prohibited; non-bank issuers are prohibited from providing credit lines or credit lines to customers to prevent stablecoins from becoming shadow banking tools; issuers must entrust independent accountants to regularly audit the assets and business operations, and report to regulators and disclose relevant information as required; all stablecoin issuers must fully connect to the anti-money laundering and cybersecurity control system and cooperate with regulatory authorities to enforce asset transfer restrictions or disposal measures in accordance with the law. Market Impact and Industry Landscape Trends Once these detailed rules are officially implemented, they will fundamentally reshape the development path of Taiwan's stablecoin market from three dimensions: entry barriers, compliance costs, and business scope. Firstly, the scarcity of licenses will increase significantly. The minimum capital requirement of NT$300 million and strict bank equity binding constraints mean that the first batch of stablecoin issuance licenses will only be open to a few leading banks and financial holding groups, resulting in a significantly higher market concentration than the ordinary virtual asset service provider sector. In the future, the local stablecoin market is unlikely to see a large number of small and medium-sized institutions competing, but rather will be dominated by a few large financial institutions with capital strength and compliance experience. Secondly, the business logic of issuers will undergo a fundamental change. The rules of full reserves, prohibition of interest payments, and localized custody of reserve assets significantly reduce the space for issuers to obtain excess returns through reserve assets. Stablecoin issuance will no longer be a high-arbitrage business, but will shift to a low-risk operating model centered on payment services and scenario ecosystems. The core competitiveness of issuers will shift from token economic design capabilities to service capabilities oriented towards the real economy, such as improving cross-border settlement efficiency, implementing supply chain payment scenarios, and building programmable payment systems. Finally, industry consolidation will accelerate during the transition period. According to the parent law, existing virtual asset service providers must submit license applications within 12 months, with a maximum approval grace period of 21 months, which can be extended to 33 months if necessary. High capital thresholds and continuous compliance investments will drive small and medium-sized platforms to gradually exit the market, concentrating industry resources on leading institutions with strong financial resources and established application scenarios. From a long-term application perspective, Taiwan's well-developed semiconductor cross-border supply chain system will provide a natural application scenario for compliant stablecoins. Traditional bank cross-border settlements are limited by business hours, time zone differences, and intermediary bank chains, making it difficult to meet the real-time settlement needs of high-frequency, small-amount cross-border trade. Compliant stablecoins pegged to mainstream fiat currencies are expected to reduce cross-border capital turnover costs for local manufacturing and trading companies in scenarios such as supply chain payments and trade finance settlements. Overall, the stablecoin regulatory details disclosed this time have chosen to classify them as "quasi-currencies" rather than "financial products," adding a central bank oversight compared to Hong Kong and an equity-based binding layer compared to the US. While opening up the legal issuance space for stablecoins, this approach maximizes the protection of financial stability and controllable monetary sovereignty. The trade-off is that the growth rate of the local stablecoin ecosystem will be relatively stable, avoiding the early, unregulated growth seen in the crypto market. Future industry development will be driven more by genuine payment needs from the real economy, rather than pure financial speculation. With the draft's public consultation period progressing and the final provisions being implemented, 2027 will be a crucial window for the official launch of the Taiwan stablecoin market.

data.title: Spain Gives Financial Watchdog Power To Freeze Crypto Accounts Without Court Approval
data.description:
Spain has granted its financial intelligence unit unequivocal power to freeze cryptocurrency accounts suspected of being linked to money laundering or terrorist financing, allowing investigators to intervene without first obtaining a court order.

Under a new royal decree-law, the country's Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses, known as Sepblac, can suspend crypto, bank and payment accounts for up to five working days. It can also halt individual transactions for up to 10 working days, with any extension requiring judicial approval.

🚨 🇪🇸 Spain is set to authorize Sepblac to freeze crypto accounts for up to five business days without prior court approval, with the new rules scheduled to take effect on January 25, 2027, pending parliamentary approval. #Spain #Crypto #Regulation #Bitcoin https://t.co/pVSfBnvdBr

— SILENT PHNIX (@silentphnix) November 26, 2026

The move marks a significant expansion of Spain's financial enforcement powers as authorities seek to prevent potentially illicit funds from disappearing before investigators can complete their inquiries.

Spain's New Decree Gives Sepblac Greater Control Over Crypto Accounts

The new measures are included in Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, a broader legislative package covering consumer credit, interest rate caps on consumer loans and the regulation of buyers of bad loans.

Spain has granted anti-laundering unit Sepblac power to freeze crypto accounts for up to 5 business days—and halt in-flight transfers for 10 days—without a judge’s prior order. Effective late Jan 2027 under RDL 44/2026: https://t.co/3sEoeCMrSk #Crypto #Spain #Regulation https://t.co/B7kUoCwuuA

— BTC Wires Official (@BTCWires) November 26, 2026

The decree introduces a new article to Spain's 2010 anti-money laundering law, authorizing Sepblac to suspend transactions in progress, block the use of bank, payment or crypto-asset accounts, and restrict business relationships when investigators identify indications of money laundering or terrorist financing.

The financial intelligence unit can use these powers to preserve potentially illicit funds while examining suspicious activity. If its suspicions are confirmed, it can then forward the relevant information to the appropriate authorities.

The decree was published in Spain's official gazette, the Boletín Oficial del Estado, on November 25, 2026.

Crypto Accounts Can Be Frozen for Five Working Days Without Court Approval

Under the new rules, Sepblac can suspend bank, payment and cryptocurrency accounts or business relationships for up to five working days. Individual transactions can be halted for a maximum of 10 working days.

🗞️ Daily Bake: Spain moves to freeze crypto accounts without a judge. Sepblac is Spain’s dirty-money unit. A decree could freeze accounts for 5 business days and block transfers for 10 days. If you use a Spanish platform, a freeze could land before a judge sees the case. https://t.co/VeQUDZtQZs

— The Builder Bakery | Web3, AI & Tech (@BuilderBakery) November 27, 2026

When suspicions arise from a suspicious activity report submitted by a bank or another financial firm, Sepblac must issue the suspension order within three working days. Authorities must also lift any suspension earlier if they determine that the restriction is no longer necessary.

Once the applicable deadlines expire, the suspension must end unless a court ratifies or extends it at the request of the public prosecutor's office. The restrictions therefore give investigators an opportunity to secure potentially criminal funds before seeking further judicial authorization, while maintaining a legal time limit on their intervention.

The European Council has put forward Pablo Hernández de Cos as next President of the European Central Bank. Once confirmed, he is expected to replace the outgoing President Christine @Lagarde on 7 February 2027. The mandate is for 8 years and non-renewable. https://t.co/kGgDBfER1B

— EU Council (@EUCouncil) November 27, 2026

The decree is scheduled to take effect on January 25, 2027, two months after its publication. As a royal decree-law, it must also receive ratification from Spain's Congress of Deputies within 30 days.

Spain Allows Financial Watchdog to Act Without Foreign Requests

Sepblac's expanded authority represents a major departure from its previous enforcement powers.

Previously, the financial intelligence unit could only suspend transactions at the request of financial intelligence units in other countries. Under the new legislation, it can initiate suspensions based on its own analysis or following requests from Spanish police.

Spain: from 25 Jan 2027, its anti-money-laundering unit Sepblac can freeze a crypto account for up to 5 business days without a court order if it suspects laundering (Royal Decree-law 44/2026). Courts must approve longer holds. #MiCA #CASP Not financial advice. https://t.co/RfmMfPnp56

— CASP Hub (@casphub) November 27, 2026

The decree also establishes legal consequences for financial firms that fail to comply with suspension orders. Companies that disregard Sepblac's instructions commit an offense under Spain's anti-money laundering law.

Meanwhile, financial institutions that comply with the orders, along with Sepblac itself, receive protection from liability for carrying out the suspensions. The Spanish government said the changes bring the country closer to standards established by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) and help implement part of the European Union's sixth anti-money laundering directive.

Authorities also pointed to the speed of digital financial transactions, arguing that potentially criminal funds can be moved before investigators have enough time to complete their analysis.

Rising Crypto Suspicious Activity Reports Put Industry Under Scrutiny

The expanded enforcement powers come as Spanish authorities face a growing number of suspicious activity reports involving cryptocurrency. According to Sepblac's latest annual report, suspicious activity reports submitted by crypto service providers increased to 1,672 in 2025, up from 972 in 2024.

Spain arrests two in Barcelona for funneling crypto to Hamas’s military wing—just one node in a sprawling international network. Europe’s politicians love crypto rhetoric but still lag on enforcement. Brussels: regulate or keep prete... https://t.co/lttmiFLgJj

— Daisy Reid (@DaisyRe80647111) November 25, 2026

The financial intelligence unit said the reports continued to expose weaknesses in how cryptocurrency firms identify the parties involved in transactions. Sepblac also identified cryptocurrency, alongside cash, as a key vulnerability for financial crime investigations because of its pseudonymous nature and the speed at which transactions can take place.

The watchdog also handled 204 requests from other European Union financial intelligence units to suspend transactions in 2025, more than double the 90 requests recorded in 2023 and up from 175 in 2024. However, the amounts involved declined to approximately €32 million ($35 million) in 2025, compared with €92 million ($101 million) in 2024. The number of affected bank accounts also fell slightly, from 316 to 307.

RIPPLE XRP: EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT VOTED 416-169 TO ADVANCE THE DIGITAL EURO? https://t.co/HtcirIfLSk

— BullrunnersHQ (@XRP_Bullrunners) November 24, 2026

Spain's expanded enforcement powers arrive ahead of its next FATF evaluation. Assessors are scheduled to conduct an on-site visit in February 2027, followed by a plenary discussion in October 2027. The FATF has previously identified peer-to-peer stablecoin transfers as a significant money laundering risk, while warning that centralized elements can still exist within decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms.

European Authorities Expand Their Powers to Target Crypto-Related Financial Crime

Spain is not alone in strengthening its ability to intervene in cryptocurrency-related financial activity, with other European countries also moving to expand enforcement powers.

In Germany, lawmakers have backed legislation granting customs authorities broader powers to seize assets, including cryptocurrency, when their lawful origins are in doubt, even if no criminal investigation is underway.

🇩🇪Germany gives customs new powers to seize crypto and other high-value assets over suspected illegal origins. The measure can apply before a criminal case begins, but permanent confiscation requires a fiscal court decision. The law targets January 1, 2027, pending Bundesrat approval.

— CoinTab News (@CoinTabNews) November 15, 2026

The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, known as Zollfinanzgerechtigkeitsgesetz, on November 12, according to the German government. Meanwhile, a taskforce convened by UK think tank RUSI has warned that cryptocurrency-related money laundering represents a significant risk ahead of the country's next FATF review.

Together, these developments highlight the growing scrutiny facing cryptocurrency transactions across Europe as governments seek stronger mechanisms to identify and disrupt suspected financial crime.

data.title: AI, US Treasury Bonds, and Bitcoin: A Battle for Liquidity
data.description:
When allocating assets, which markets are worth participating in? When to participate and when to exit? These are questions we need to consider frequently when investing. Amidst constant talk of "AI bubble" and "Fed rate hikes," what truly determines asset price fluctuations? Today, we'll attempt to explore this question. I. Three Major Markets, One Main Theme Amidst the backdrop of Sino-US competition, we currently focus on only three major market categories: A-shares, US stocks, and non-sovereign markets (cryptocurrency, gold, etc.). US stocks represent the world's most advanced technology, A-shares represent global manufacturing capabilities, and non-sovereign markets meet hedging needs. Although China has strict foreign exchange controls, this only slows down the flow of funds—meaning that fluctuations in the capital market are essentially just the movement of liquidity between different markets. Gold is very familiar to everyone, but Bitcoin makes it easier to see the full picture: The subprime mortgage crisis of 2007–2008 led to massive bank failures and the government using huge sums of taxpayer money to bail out financial institutions. On September 15, 2008, Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy protection, and the crisis escalated rapidly; subsequently, the United States passed the Emergency Economic Stabilization Act for a large-scale bailout. This exposed the fragility of the traditional financial system: relying on "trusted third parties" (banks, central banks) not only brings the risk of single points of failure but also moral hazard and excessive money supply. People's trust in governments and central banks declined sharply. Bitcoin emerged in this context—it attempts to build an electronic cash system that does not rely on any central institution and does not require trust in third parties. In other words, the background for Bitcoin's existence, or rather, the fundamental driving force behind its rise, as a decentralized monetary system, is the continuous over-issuance of fiat currency in the global system. Therefore, we often see that in relatively loose financial environments, such as when the Federal Reserve cuts interest rates or engages in quantitative easing, Bitcoin can outperform other markets, rising several times or even dozens of times more than other mainstream markets. This is also the reason why Bitcoin has created a large amount of wealth in past cycles. II. AI and Crypto: On the Same Table On January 20, 2025, Trump was sworn in as the 47th President of the United States in the Rotunda of the Capitol Building in Washington, D.C. To circumvent the limitations of his presidential status, Trump launched his own coin, TRUMPP, just three days before his official inauguration, potentially marking a significant turning point. While cryptocurrency became a matter of interest for the Trump family, AI also became a top priority for Trump's second term. To this end, Trump specifically created an advisory role, with David Sacks coordinating AI and crypto policies. In October 2026, he established the Super Intelligence Force (SIF), primarily to coordinate the federal government and ensure America's leading position in the field of "superintelligence" (renamed AI by the Trump administration). Furthermore, Trump promoted a massive AI infrastructure boom in the US through various means, including government equity investments, the chip bill, and attracting foreign investment and factory construction. Although the Republican Party lost in the midterm elections, the strong economic growth driven by Trump and the Republican Party is undeniable. In a previous article, I mentioned the significant differences in AI development between China and the US. A crucial point is that the US is dominated by the private sector: companies raise ever-increasing funds for AI development by issuing new shares and bonds, and the intermediaries for these financing needs are all core US private financial institutions. Because of early optimism about AI development, with the industry perceived as having high certainty and profit margins, both large companies and emerging smaller companies like Neocloud saw their fundraising scale increase year by year, even accelerating, offering higher yields than US Treasury bonds—generally above 7% in the early stages. However, as everyone knows, AI development is a bottomless pit, with short-term funding needs in the trillions and long-term needs in the tens of trillions.

III. AI Corporate Bonds and US Treasuries "Competing for Funds"

Thus, a situation has arisen where AI corporate bonds are competing with US Treasury bonds for funds. Without considering risks, or assuming AI corporate bonds receive high ratings and endorsements from institutions, investors are happy to invest in these bonds. At this time, US Treasury bonds experience a massive sell-off, causing yields to soar. As a result, the total amount of US Treasury bonds quickly exceeded $40 trillion, and the interest burden has become unbearable.

The rest of the story is probably familiar to everyone: voices about the bursting of the AI ​​bubble have been rising one after another, and the market has shown various "adverse reactions"—the credit spreads (CDS) of AI corporate bonds have soared rapidly, the Nasdaq index in the US stock market has fluctuated abnormally, and after the midterm elections, it finally turned downwards and entered a technical bear market. There was even a dramatic turn of events, with Huang Jingyu embroiled in controversy, resigning and then being reinstated. This inevitably raises suspicions that the Ministry of Finance is manipulating things behind the scenes. Those interested can read a parable I wrote last time; it's quite interesting.

IV. The Biggest Victim: Bitcoin

At this point, readers may not have noticed that, against the backdrop of this fierce competition for funds, one asset has become the biggest victim—Bitcoin.

Theoretically, the United States has consistently been in a state of excessive money printing. With the total US debt exceeding $41 trillion, the credibility of the US dollar has become increasingly precarious. Bitcoin, as the opposite of fiat currency, has every reason to absorb the liquidity of the US dollar and achieve a better development situation. Some may ask why not gold—because gold is a global asset, while Bitcoin is a US dollar asset. We can discuss this topic another time.

Let's use some data to illustrate this more clearly:

Currently, MicroStrategy, the largest buyer of Bitcoin, is raising funds from the market by issuing perpetual preferred stock, offering a yield of 12% to 16%, to purchase Bitcoin.

Hyperscalers like Meta, Google, and Amazon raise massive amounts of capital to invest in AI development by issuing corporate bonds with yields around 7%; Neoclouds like CoreWeave, on the other hand, have seen their yields soar to over 10%. The U.S. Treasury raises its operating funds by issuing 1-year bonds at 4.57%, 10-year bonds at 4.85%, and 30-year bonds at 5.24%, yields that represent the market's "risk-free benchmark."

For details, please see the image below:

This doesn't consider other yield products for now. Just from the yields offered by these three main categories of products, you can feel the intensity of the competition for funds in the market. I haven't even mentioned the siphoning of market liquidity by the three giants: SpaceX, Anthropic, and OpenAI.

V. A Liquidity Crisis Without Gunfire

So, why is this Nasdaq crash unprecedented in decades? Why did Bitcoin go from bull to bear? Why has the A-share market been unable to break through 4000 points? Why can Nvidia's market capitalization fluctuate by trillions in a single day? — The reason lies in the fact that the entire capital market is already stretched thin. On the one hand, we can feel the booming development of AI, but on the other hand, we are constrained by tight liquidity.

At this moment, you will find that no financial sector has collapsed, the Federal Reserve has not (and will not) aggressively raise interest rates, corporate financial statements still look good and performance is growing rapidly, but at this very moment we are experiencing a liquidity crisis.

The US-Iran conflict and the inflation caused by AI development have become a Damocles' sword hanging over the Federal Reserve, forcing it to raise interest rates again—is it really necessary to force the Fed to comply by creating a stock market crash? Bitcoin's role as currency has never changed, but its role as an asset faces fierce global competition for liquidity. Trump attempted to use AI and cryptocurrency as a powerful weapon to create a brilliant second term, but while AI boosted US GDP, it failed to help him win the midterm elections; and cryptocurrency may become the biggest stain on his career. The global capital market is a game of chess: where liquidity goes, prices rise; where there is more liquidity, there are greater wealth opportunities. We'll share more about how to break this liquidity crisis later. Feel free to leave a comment and tell us whether you've made a profit or a loss in this current volatile liquidity environment.

data.title: Bitcoin Core Privacy Leak Puts Wallet Users At Risk As A 34-Cent Payment Can Reveal Their IP Addresses
data.description:
A Bitcoin privacy weakness could allow attackers to identify the internet addresses of computers monitoring Bitcoin wallets for as little as 18 cents.

The method takes advantage of how Bitcoin Core automatically resends unconfirmed transactions, potentially allowing an observer to connect a Bitcoin address to the network connection of the computer tracking it.

Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail disclosed the issue in a post on the Delving Bitcoin developer forum on 25 November 2026.

Although the attack has only been tested on a separate network, its low cost and reported accuracy have raised concerns about the privacy of Bitcoin wallet users and node operators.

How Can A Payment Reveal A Bitcoin User's IP Address?

The attack exploits a feature in Bitcoin Core that automatically rebroadcasts wallet transactions if they remain unconfirmed for approximately 12 to 36 hours.

This process helps transactions reach other nodes and eventually get included in the blockchain.

Ismail found that an attacker could deliberately trigger this behaviour by sending a tiny payment to a Bitcoin address that has already been used.

By setting the transaction fee at the lowest amount accepted by the network, the attacker can make the payment unlikely to be confirmed.

A Bitcoin Core developer outlined a way to identify the IP address behind a BTC wallet for less than $0.35

Abubakar Sadiq Ismail demonstrated an attack that links a wallet address to a node's IP address

It exploits a built-in feature: wallets automatically rebroadcast… pic.twitter.com/sNezCdXOxL

— Byte Beard (@Byte_Beard) November 26, 2026

After waiting roughly a day, the attacker monitors connected Bitcoin nodes to identify which one rebroadcasts the transaction.

Since the wallet tracking that address is responsible for sending it again, the attacker can potentially identify the node's IP address and link it to the wallet.

Each attempt is estimated to cost between $0.18 and $0.34, based on Bitcoin trading at approximately $60,000.

This makes the method relatively inexpensive to repeat.

Tests Identify The Correct Node In All 30 Attempts

Ismail tested the technique 30 times on a separate network running standard Bitcoin Core software, successfully identifying the correct node in all 30 attempts.

However, the results have not yet been measured on Bitcoin's live network, meaning the reported accuracy does not establish how reliably the attack would work under real-world conditions.

The exposure also extends beyond users running Bitcoin Core's built-in wallets.

Other wallet software that relies on Core to monitor transactions could be affected, including Sparrow in Core mode, Specter, Liana, JoinMarket and Electrum Personal Server.

Even users who believe they have protected their connections with Tor may remain exposed.

Nodes that use Tor alongside regular internet connections can still reveal their real IP addresses because the transaction rebroadcast is sent through both types of connections.

Tor-Only Connections And Manual Broadcasting Offer Protection

The attack depends on a node maintaining connections to the regular internet, commonly known as clearnet.

Users can reduce this exposure by configuring Bitcoin Core with the -onlynet=onion setting, which restricts network communications to Tor connections.

Nodes configured with -onlynet=onion have a smaller attack surface. This parameter forces all node communication through Tor, eliminating clearnet connections that could otherwise be monitored.

— Wall Street Peak (@WallStreetPeak) November 27, 2026

Another option is to disable automatic wallet broadcasting through -walletbroadcast=0.

However, this means users must send their transactions to the network manually rather than allowing the software to broadcast them automatically.

The issue does not involve stolen funds or compromised private keys.

Instead, it concerns the ability to connect a Bitcoin wallet to an identifiable internet connection, potentially weakening the privacy users expect when managing their holdings.

Bitcoin Core Developers Disagree Over The Proposed Fix

A proposed code change, PR #36482, aims to reduce the exposure by limiting automatic rebroadcasting to transactions newly added to a node's memory pool, which stores transactions waiting for confirmation.

However, fellow Bitcoin Core contributor Martin Zumsande argued that the adjustment would not sufficiently address the problem, saying it "only raises the cost of the active attack slightly".

Zumsande also recommended making the rebroadcasting of incoming transactions an opt-in feature, meaning users would have to enable it themselves.

PR #36482 has not been released, while the proposed opt-in alternatives are being discussed separately under PR #36398 and PR #36481.

There have been no reports of widespread exploitation so far.

Until developers agree on a fix, users relying on Bitcoin Core wallets with regular internet connections may need to review their network settings and transaction broadcasting preferences.
